claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself.
A Pulumi component state migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi component state migrations are new.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A GitHub discussion for component state migrations feedback exists at pulumi/pulumi discussions/24799.
A Pulumi docs guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering the callback contract.
The pulumi/examples repo contains an aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration example with three programs (v1, v2, v3) and migration code.

The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, creating a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway, with a security group outside the component referring to the VPC.
Replacing an AWS VPC requires replacing a security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId docs).
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data.
The v2 example upgrades to the modern `awsx.ec2.Vpc` component while keeping the existing network.
The v3 example removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

The resource trees Pulumi tracks: v1 has awsx:x:ec2:Vpc with Subnet and InternetGateway component wrappers; v2 has awsx:ec2:Vpc with managed aws resources beneath the VPC and subnet named vpc-isolated-1; v3 has plain aws resources only.
Pulumi state records both physical resources and components; each record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a cloud provider ID.
The legacy AWSX component wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, while modern AWSX removes those wrappers and puts managed resources under different parents.
In the example, the Pulumi name of the subnet changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1` between legacy and modern AWSX.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but do not remove component wrappers and transfer references.
Pulumi component resources accept a `stateMigrations` option that registers migration callbacks, used alongside an alias for the legacy component type.
The migration callback receives the aliased old component's saved state followed by the state of its children.

The migration callback returns `newState` (the complete set of records replacing the old component and its children) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to the URN that replaces it).
The example migration returns without changes if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources, and raises an error on an unexpected component type.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record, changes its URN, type, and parent, and preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Pulumi uses `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid with the same AWS VPC ID.
The second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and maps both the old component and its VPC child to the new VPC record, which keeps its AWS ID.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration, and after both have run both callbacks return no result.
After a migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
`pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.
In the example upgrade, the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group should show no creates, deletes, or replacements in preview.

When users upgrade a component that registers a migration, Pulumi runs the migration automatically as part of the normal preview and update without users writing the migration, attaching the callback, or editing stack state.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the state migrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration callback is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.

A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings, where each mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi state migration callback state entries use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as `urn`, `type`, `id`, `parent`, `provider`, `inputs`, and `outputs`.
The Pulumi resource options reference page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/ has a 'callback-api' section explaining the callback API.
A Pulumi state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing results of Pulumi state migrations (with update plans or targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
